chapter: Uptown clubs and the Black Cat
title: Switching from banjo to guitar
summary: The club manager told him to get a guitar, which he bought on time at King's on 47th Street.

story.theme_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section: instruments and players
story.community_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section's changing role

blocks.x: No. That's when I say I was playing the banjo, and the guy -- the manager of the club said -- 'Well -- everybody's playing guitar now. You have to -- (laugh) -- you have to get the guitar, okay? real quick*.
Did you?
Yeah, I got one.
Where? From a pawn shop or something?
No. I got one from -- there used to be a music store on 47th -- 47th Street. Right across the street there, called King's. King's Music Store. I think that was the name of it.
Not the ["trumpet"] Kings?
I really don't know. But, there was a music store there.
Yeah.
And I bought this guitar there, and I started playing over at the -- because I bought it on time, more or less, I didn't --(Laugh)
Yeah. Yeah.
Well the pawn shops must have been loaded with banjos around.
Oh, yeah. Yeah. Listen, the change-over, you know, from the banjo --
Yeah.
It was something, you know, it was so abrupt as far as I'm concerned.
Yeah.
Yeah. Well, wasn't it partly that microphones were coming in?
It could have been. I don't know.
Weren't they? Stan, weren't they?
I don't know the reason, but --
Because, you see, if they were then you could afford to play a guitar because the whole thing was reproduced better.
Mm hmm. Mm hmm.
I guess that had something to do with it.
Yeah. It could have.
Yeah. I think so. I mean, guys stopped using megaphones?
Yes, yes. Yes.
So they were singing into something.
Yes. Yes.
I think, though, that they -- I think the thing was that they -- it wasn't entirely that. I think they decided that the guitar was a more musical sound, didn't they?
Yes. I think so.
